reviews.author: Brent Marchant
reviews.content: Romances involving partners in love engaged in crime sprees aren’t especially new or original. In fact, sagas of outlaws on the run have been film industry staples for decades, perhaps best exemplified by the legendary “Bonnie and Clyde” (1967). So, considering the prevalence of these films, it takes a lot to make new offerings in this genre stand out and distinguish themselves. That’s where the latest feature from director Adam Carter Rehmeier comes into play. While this release very much follows the typical formula of these pictures, it manages to separate itself from its peers in a number of ways. At the same time, though, it also tips its hat to the aforementioned “Bonnie and Clyde,” as well as to such other crime/outlaw thrillers as “Thelma & Louise” (1991), “The Sugarland Express” (1974) and “The Grifters” (1990). The film follows the transformation of Caroline Daniels (Samara Weaving), who’s stuck in a dead-end filling station job in small town Texas. Her life changes drastically, however, when con artist Oliver Anderson (Kyle Gallner) storms into town and sweeps Caroline off her feet. They launch into a torrid romance while Oliver teaches her the ways of grifting from both practical and psychological standpoints. And, before long, they leave Texas, embarking on a road trip across the Southeast during which she adeptly learns the art of the con from her mentor/lover. Given their success as a duo, they quickly up the ante of the jobs, from pickpocketing and simple obfuscation routines to include identity theft and bank robbery. They use their newly acquired ample funds to adopt a more lavish lifestyle as they make their way (at Caroline’s request) to Charleston, South Carolina, where she hopes to look up her long-estranged mother, Deborah (Kyra Sedgwick). But, when Caroline is left disillusioned by the disastrous meeting between her and her crusty, self-absorbed mom, she rashly decides that she wants to amass enough money as quickly as possible to leave the US permanently, a decision that carries devastatingly serious consequences. Much of this is admittedly rather predictable, but it’s nonetheless stylish in its execution, featuring fine performances (especially Weaving and Sedgwick), clever film editing, a revealing inside look into the ways of scammers, a hefty dose of unadulterated Americana and a decidedly pronounced 1970s vibe, qualities that give the film character all its own. However, with that said, it’s also important to note that there some notable anachronisms here that take the 1970s vibe a little too far (who knew there were still that many pay phones left), along with an opening half hour whose pacing could decidedly stand to be stepped up. In addition, while the script openly and specifically addresses hypothetical questions related to our own innate senses of good and evil, how they come to pass, and how such attitudes might shift, Caroline’s metamorphosis here seems a bit extreme and overly quick given who she appears to be at the story’s outset, a character development issue that comes across as exaggeratedly accelerated. However, in the overall context of the picture, these shortcomings are easy to overlook, particularly when the intensity of the narrative amps up in the second half. “Carolina Caroline” may not be especially innovative or groundbreaking as movies of this stripe go, but it is nevertheless entertaining and engaging, and there’s definitely no crime in that.

aiEnrichment.summary_one_sentence: Desperate to escape her dead-end small town, a young Texas woman hits the road with a charismatic con man on a crime-filled journey across the Southeast to find her estranged mother.
aiEnrichment.summary_short: Caroline Daniels feels trapped in her quiet Texas life, caring for her father while longing for something more. When she catches a charming drifter named Oliver running a scam at her workplace, she convinces him to take her along and teach her his trickster ways. Their mentorship quickly turns into a passionate romance as they travel across the American Southeast, pulling off small-time hustles and armed bank robberies. However, as their criminal spree escalates and Caroline's search for her mother yields painful truths, their thrilling getaway turns into a high-stakes struggle for survival.
aiEnrichment.summary_long: In a sleepy Texas town, gas station attendant Caroline Daniels dreams of leaving her quiet life behind to reconnect with her long-absent mother in South Carolina. Her world changes when Oliver, a slick and worldly con artist, attempts a short-change scam at her store. Intrigued rather than alarmed, Caroline clocks his trick and demands to join him on the road. Oliver agrees to teach her the art of the hustle, and as they travel through the American Southeast, their criminal partnership evolves into a passionate, whirlwind romance. What begins as petty theft and clever cons quickly escalates into higher-stakes armed bank robberies. Tension begins to surface when Oliver displays a darker, more dangerous side during a heist, leaving Caroline conflicted about their increasingly volatile path. When they finally reach South Carolina, Caroline's reunion with her mother proves devastatingly painful, pushing her to double down on their illegal ambitions to escape the country altogether. Their lawbreaking ultimately catches up with them, leading to a fateful confrontation with law enforcement that changes their lives forever.
aiEnrichment.synopsis: Set against the backdrop of the sweltering American South, 'Carolina Caroline' follows Caroline Daniels, a young woman seeking escape from the monotony of her rural Texas hometown. When she crosses paths with Oliver, an elusive and charming drifter who pulls off small-time cons, she recognizes an opportunity for freedom. Striking up an unlikely partnership, Caroline joins Oliver on a road trip heading toward South Carolina, where she hopes to locate the estranged mother who abandoned her as an infant. Along the way, Oliver instructs Caroline in the mechanics of deception and hustle, and their shared thrill kindles an intense, romantic connection. As their ambitions grow, the duo moves from petty schemes to daring bank robberies, attracting heat from authorities and putting their bond to the test. Balancing high-octane suspense with grounded romantic drama, the film explores themes of intimacy, desperation, and the search for identity through the lens of a classic Southern crime adventure.
